verdict: Amazon's sales rose 10% to $148.0B and operating income nearly doubled to $14.7B as AWS grew 19% and earned $9.3B — and it kept $13.5B as profit.

segments.name: North America
segments.note: Stores, subscriptions and ads in North America — the biggest piece, and it earned a $5.1B operating profit.

segments.name: International
segments.note: The same businesses outside North America — swung to a $0.3B operating profit after a $0.9B loss a year earlier.

segments.name: AWS
segments.note: Cloud computing rented to other companies — grew 19%, and its $9.3B operating profit was 64% of Amazon's total.

opex.name: Fulfillment
opex.note: Running the warehouses and delivering packages — the biggest single running cost.

opex.name: Technology & infrastructure
opex.note: Servers, data centers, and the engineers who build and run the products.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Advertising Amazon's products and winning customers.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Back office — finance, legal and management.

opex.name: Other operating expense, net
opex.note: Small net charges that do not fit the other lines.

otherDetail: Interest income $1,180M, less $589M interest expense and $18M of other expense, net — the non-operating lines include a $0.4B pre-tax gain on Amazon's stake in Rivian; a $7M equity-method gain is recorded below the tax line.
follow100Note: AWS alone earned $9.3B of operating profit — 64% of Amazon's total — on just $17.76 of every $100 of sales. The rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: AWS kept accelerating
takeaways.text: AWS sales grew 19% to $26.3B and the segment earned $9.3B of operating profit — 64% of Amazon's total — as companies moved more computing, and new AI work, onto its cloud.

takeaways.title: Operating income nearly doubled
takeaways.text: Consolidated operating income rose 91% from a year ago: North America earned $5.1B and International swung from a $0.9B loss to a $0.3B profit as the store networks got more efficient.

takeaways.title: Profit doubled
takeaways.text: Net income doubled to $13.5B from $6.7B a year ago; about $0.4B of it was a paper gain on Amazon's investment in electric-truck maker Rivian, recorded before tax.

oneTimers: A $0.4B pre-tax paper gain on Amazon's common-stock investment in Rivian Automotive sits inside non-operating income — it is a revaluation of shares Amazon owns, not money from customers.
